title: Pulse, ECG and breathing
summary: The pulse at a fingertip (a photoplethysmogram) with the ECG and breathing.
description: A pulse oximeter's photoplethysmogram (PPG) shows how much light the blood in a fingertip absorbs: it rises with each pulse of blood. It is shown with the ECG and with breathing, recorded from the electrical impedance across the chest (the trace is cut off at its top), in a patient in intensive care. Each pulse reaches the finger a short time after the QRS that started it, and the size of the pulses rises and falls with breathing. The small marks on the breathing trace are breaths, marked by hand.
look_for: The time from an R wave to the foot of the pulse that follows it (the pulse arrival time)
The breathing rate: count the breaths in a minute
How the pulses grow and shrink with breathing
